subject: Science
question_short_text: Inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW)
text: Who among the following is considered as the inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW)?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist, invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN. He developed the foundational protocols (HTTP, HTML, URI/URL) and the first web browser and server that became the basis for the modern web.

research.summary: Tim Berners-Lee's invention of the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN was a deliberate synthesis of existing technologies—hypertext, the Internet, and TCP/DNS protocols—rather than a fundamentally new technology. The trap this question tests is recognizing that the other three options are associated with entirely different domains of technology. Edward Kasner was a mathematician famous for coining 'googol' and 'googolplex,' terms used in mathematics and later by Google for its search engine, but he had no connection to the web. Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft and revolutionized personal computing through operating systems and software, but Microsoft was not the developer of the web. Vinod Dham is an Indian-American engineer known as the 'Father of the Pentium Chip' for his crucial work on Intel's microprocessor development, which enabled computing power but was entirely separate from web technology. Berners-Lee's unique contribution was envisioning that hypertext could be connected to the Internet to create a system for information sharing among scientists at CERN. His proposal came in March 1989, and by 1990-1991, he had written the first HTTP server, the first web browser (WorldWideWeb.app), and published the foundational specifications for HTML and HTTP. Critically, Berners-Lee ensured the web remained open and royalty-free, refusing to proprietary lock it, which enabled its explosive global adoption starting in 1991. This open philosophy was foundational to why the web became universal rather than remaining a closed system. He was knighted in 2004 and received the 2016 Turing Award for this invention.
facts: Berners-Lee invented the web at CERN (European Particle Physics Laboratory) in 1989 to solve the problem of information-sharing among geographically dispersed scientists from over 100 countries.
The first web server went live in December 1991 at Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC), and the public internet announcement occurred in August 1991, spreading the technology globally.

The three foundational technologies Berners-Lee created and standardized were HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), HTML (HyperText Markup Language), and URIs/URLs (Uniform Resource Identifiers), which form the technical backbone of all websites today.

Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina's Mosaic browser (1993) was the first user-friendly graphical web browser that accelerated mass adoption; Berners-Lee's original browser was simpler and ran only on NeXT computers.
Berners-Lee founded the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) in 1994 at MIT to maintain open standards and prevent proprietary fragmentation of web technologies.
